answer.rationale: Competitor price-cut pressure creates urgency, but exp_73 definitively shows targeted discounting fails on retention—the acquired cohort does not survive renewal, making it unsustainable despite short-term acquisition lift. Promotional pricing is therefore contraindicated. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for established customers but don't address churn in price-sensitive SMB accounts already at risk. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is misaligned to the immediate SMB churn problem. Activation messaging (memory_91, exp_91) and onboarding simplification (memory_86, memory_31) both improve early engagement and retention without revenue loss. Activation messaging was confirmed on exp_91 with +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, and +1% retention—a durable signal. A standard experiment deploying in-product activation messaging targeted at churning SMB accounts offers the highest-confidence path to re-engage price-sensitive cohorts on value, not price, while preserving long-term retention and sustainable revenue. This addresses the competitor threat defensively without sacrificing unit economics.
